questions.q: What is described as the single biggest lever an App Builder has over user experience?
options: Adding more fields so every detail is captured
Reducing the number of actions between needing to do something and having it done
Increasing the number of validation rules per object
Using more chart types on the dashboard
questions.explain: Every extra click or field a user has to work around is friction, and friction is why people route around a well-built app with a spreadsheet instead of adopting it.

questions.q: Which feature shows only the fields relevant to a record's current state, instead of one long static layout?
options: Dynamic Forms
Roll-up summary fields
Change sets
Permission set groups
questions.explain: Dynamic Forms (introduced in Lesson 9) conditionally display fields based on the record's state, directly reducing the clutter a user has to scroll past.

questions.q: What does Salesforce's Optimizer app help an App Builder identify?
options: Which Apex classes have the fastest execution time
The exact dollar cost of each Salesforce license
Which sandbox types are available in the org
Signs of a build that shipped but didn't land — unused fields, inactive validation rules, and similar adoption gaps
questions.explain: Optimizer surfaces exactly the kind of evidence — unused fields, inactive rules — that separates a deployed feature from an adopted one.

questions.q: What rollout approach does this lesson recommend over flipping a switch for everyone at once?
options: Deploying directly to production with no sandbox testing
Disabling the app for managers until all reps have used it
Phasing the rollout by assigning the new app's permission set to a pilot group first, gathering feedback, then expanding
Skipping training entirely and relying on in-app guidance alone
questions.explain: A phased rollout by permission set lets a pilot group surface real problems before the whole organization is exposed to them.

questions.q: Why does this lesson prefer training on 'the workflow' over training on 'the feature list'?
options: Feature lists are faster to write
Workflow training replaces the need for field-level help text
Salesforce requires workflow-based training for certification
Workflow-based training (e.g. 'here's how you log a visit') maps to how users actually think about their job, rather than an abstract inventory of every field
questions.explain: Training framed around the task a user is trying to accomplish lands better than an exhaustive walkthrough of every field on an object.
